question: In a trial, 40 of 100 patients on a pill improve, against 30 of 100 on a dummy. How many improved because of the pill?
answer: 40 − 30 = 10 patients helped by the pill itself.
move: Credit a cause only with what changed beyond what happened anyway.
ask: When something I tried seemed to work, how many of those good days would have come anyway?
trap: Crediting the pill with all 40 who got better.
hint: Ask what the dummy-pill group shows would have happened anyway.
steps: Would have improved anyway, as the dummy group shows: 30 of 100.
40 − 30 = 10 patients helped by the pill itself.
reference: Evans, Thornton, Chalmers & Glasziou, Testing Treatments: Better Research for Better Healthcare, 2nd ed., Pinter & Martin, 2011
